- [medium] src/collector/listening_ports.rs:207 — Every socket-table read error is skipped, so an unreadable TCP table alongside a readable UDP table produces a partial snapshot that replaces the known-good one. Impact: existing TCP listeners appear removed. Fix: skip only absent optional IPv6 tables and propagate other read errors.
- [medium] src/known_set.rs:406 — The representative process is updated without its `deleted` flag, so an old deleted image and its running replacement can report different flags depending on enumeration order. Fix: keep representative-specific flags with the selected process and test both input orders.
- [medium] src/incident/diff.rs:115 — Process-controlled names and paths are written into `diff.md` without escaping, so a newline in a process name can create fake headings or findings. Impact: the investigator reads forged evidence. Fix: escape Markdown and control characters in displayed entries and keep raw values in the JSON.
- [medium] build.ps1:5 — The script copies executables into `built/bin/` without creating that directory, and no tracked file creates it, so the copy fails on a clean checkout. Fix: create the staging and installation directories before copying.
- [medium] src/collector/processes.rs:14 — The collector excludes only `own_root` and not running investigations, which `classify_processes` does at src/commands.rs:327-328, so the diff and the classification can disagree. Impact: investigation processes appear and disappear in every incident diff. Fix: pass `investigation::running(paths, &processes)` into the exclusions, or share one helper.
- [medium] src/collector/processes.rs:44 — `instances` is written into the snapshot, and it changes constantly for processes such as chrome.exe and svchost.exe. Impact: `diff.md` shows changes in every incident. Fix: drop it from the snapshot or mark it volatile with `is_volatile_key`.
- [medium] src/collector/listening_ports.rs:200 — On Linux, UDP state `07` matches every unconnected socket, including short-lived ephemeral-port client sockets, and the Windows UDP table at line 152 likewise lists every bound endpoint. Impact: random UDP keys are added and removed in each diff, which can hide a real new listener. Fix: filter ephemeral UDP ports or leave UDP out of the diff key.
- [medium] src/incident/unknown.rs:122 — When `/proc/<pid>/exe` is unavailable, the code strips ` (deleted)` and hashes the original pathname, which after an upgrade can name the replacement binary. Impact: the incident gets a valid SHA-256 for the wrong executable. Fix: hash only a verified reference to the original image, or record why the hash is unavailable.
- [medium] src/probe/process.rs:154 — The Linux `stat` record must be valid UTF-8, so a valid non-UTF-8 process name drops the whole process even when its PID and executable path are readable. Fix: parse the record as bytes and decode only the display name lossily.

fix: keep wrong or spoofed details out of unknown-process evidence

- Command lines and /proc/<pid>/exe are looked up by PID after the
  classification, so a reused PID attached another process's details.
  The processes are enumerated before and after reading, and values
  read by PID are kept only when the same PID and start time appear
  both times.
- For a deleted executable, the original path with " (deleted)"
  stripped was hashed as a fallback, which after an upgrade is the
  replacement binary. Only /proc/<pid>/exe is tried now.
- Bidi control characters passed through to the summary table, so a
  name could display reversed (e.g. a fake ".txt"). They are removed
  along with the other control characters; the JSON keeps raw values.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

The second review is running in the background. Here is what has happened so far.

## Round 1 results and fixes
The review returned 15 findings (3 high, 10 medium, 2 low) and asked for changes. Of those, I fixed the 13 that were in the code and committed them as 8 commits. On Windows, clippy passes and all tests pass: 274 unit and 12 e2e.

| Commit | What it fixes |
|---|---|
| f099e9a | Fixes two ways an alert could be lost. The first is when the expression flips to false on the re-run classification (e.g. `missing >= 1 && unknown == 0`). The second is when a failed process enumeration was treated as recovery |
| 286feb8 | The `deleted` flag could come from a process other than the representative |
| 01808bf | The processes snapshot now excludes running investigations, so the snapshot and the classification no longer disagree. Instance counts are no longer compared in the diff |
| 1b95fb2 | `listening_ports`: a partial read failure no longer counts as success, UDP ephemeral ports are grouped under `ephemeral`, and every owner of a shared socket is listed |
| 2ec5649 | If the PID was reused, another process's command line and hash are no longer attached. The replacement file is no longer hashed for a deleted executable. Characters that reverse the display direction are removed from the table |
| e7e4a08 | Process names can no longer forge headings or items in `diff.md` |
| 2ba2bf3 | A Linux process whose name isn't valid UTF-8 no longer drops out of the process list |

## Findings I didn't fix
These two aren't in the branch's commits. They point at files in the working tree that I didn't write, so I left them alone.
- **`build.ps1` (high and medium):** before replacing the binaries, it deletes every file in the install folder, and it never creates the folder it copies into.
- **`.entire/settings.json` (high):** the review settings are read from the checkout under review, so the branch being reviewed can change its own review instructions.

I expect round 2 to flag these again. If you want them fixed, tell me and I'll handle them.

## Other notes
- **The review results weren't posted to the trail.** The trail API returned "repository not found (404)", so the results are only on this machine.
- **I haven't confirmed the Linux code even compiles.** Several fixes this round touch Linux-only code. To check, it has to be built in WSL, which needs free space on C:. If you're OK with that, I'll check it there.

When round 2 finishes, I'll fix any new findings and run the review again.

request changes: the installer can delete installed files, and process, port, and incident evidence has several attribution and correctness gaps.

- [high] build.ps1:8 — Deletes every file in the installed `bin` directory before either replacement is in place, which removes separately installed runtime DLLs and leaves Kuda unusable if the move fails. Fix: stage and verify `kuda.exe` and `kudaw.exe`, replace only those two files, and keep the previous pair on failure.
- [high] src/incident/unknown.rs:128 — After PID verification fails, a pathname-based SHA-256 is still attached to the process, so if the executable is replaced after the process exits, the incident records the replacement's hash for the original process. Fix: hash a handle bound to the observed image, or record the hash as unavailable.
- [medium] src/commands.rs:215 — The trigger streak is preserved on every failed enumeration whose expression does not match; for `loss == 0 && missing >= 1`, a failure makes `loss == 0` definitely false, yet matches on either side still count as consecutive. Fix: preserve state only when evaluation is unknown, and reset on a definite false.
- [medium] src/collector/listening_ports.rs:32 — Every UDP port in the dynamic range is replaced with `ephemeral`, so two listeners of the same executable on one address collapse into one record and closing one produces no diff. Fix: keep numeric ports in the snapshot and apply noise suppression only when rendering the diff.
- [medium] src/collector/listening_ports.rs:47 — `probe::enumerate().unwrap_or_default()` turns a failed enumeration into empty owners, so every listener renders `"processes": ["unknown"]` and the collector still reports success, producing false diffs or storing bad last-known-good data. Fix: propagate the error, as the `/proc/net` path does.
- [medium] src/collector/processes.rs:52 — Name and user come from the lowest-PID representative of each identity, so `diff.md` shows spurious changes such as `user: root ⇒ alice` when that representative exits. Fix: record the sorted set of distinct names and users per identity.
- [medium] src/probe/process.rs:172 — Linux start time is derived from wall-clock `btime`, which can shift by 1 s between enumerations; the exact equality checks in `investigation::running` (src/investigation.rs:62), `without_descendants`, and `enrich` (src/incident/unknown.rs:124) then fail, so a running `kuda diagnose` is not excluded and valid hashes and command lines are dropped. Fix: compare start ticks on Linux, or allow ±1 s.

content.text:
Round 3 of the review is running in the background.

The second review also asked for changes, with 14 findings. 12 were in code, and I fixed all of them in 9 commits. The other 2 were the same `build.ps1` findings as round 1, so I left them alone. On Windows, fmt, clippy and the full test suite all pass (278 unit, 12 e2e).

| Commit | What it fixes |
|---|---|
| e42919f | A failed process enumeration now keeps the trigger state only when the expression can't be decided. If the expression is definitely false, the consecutive-match streak resets |
| d5687cb | Start times within ±1 second count as the same process. On Linux, the computed start time can shift by 1 second between enumerations, so a running investigation sometimes failed to be excluded |
| 302f51f | A hash or command line is attached only when the same PID, start time and path are seen both before and after reading. Hash reads are capped at 1 GiB per incident |
| 9826495 | `listening_ports` keeps UDP ephemeral port numbers as evidence while leaving them out of the diff. A failed process enumeration now fails the collector, and listeners owned by kuda or a running investigation are excluded |
| 81b1e75 | The `processes` snapshot records every name, path and user within an identity, so a change of representative process no longer produces a diff |
| db8fa1c | Linux kernel threads are now detected by the kernel-thread flag rather than by "PID 2". Inside a PID namespace, PID 2 can be an ordinary service |
| fddb0e0 | Linux paths that aren't valid UTF-8 no longer collapse into the same identity |

Most of the fixes in rounds 1 and 2 are in Linux-only code, and I still haven't confirmed that code even compiles. Building it in WSL would need free space on C:, so tell me if you're OK with me doing that.

When round 3 finishes, I'll report its results.

Generating final report with Claude Code...
request changes: the build script can delete unrelated installed files, and several process-watch paths can misidentify processes, misattribute evidence, or drop data.

- [high] build.ps1:8 — deletes every file in the installed bin directory before moving replacements, so unrelated files are lost and a failed move leaves Kuda unavailable; stage both executables first and replace only kuda.exe and kudaw.exe.
- [medium] build.ps1:5 — copies into built/bin, which is absent from a clean checkout, so the copy fails before installation; create the staging and install directories explicitly before copying.
- [medium] src/probe/process.rs:219 — lossy UTF-8 maps distinct invalid process names to the same replacement character, so a new process inherits a known status when the executable path is unreadable; keep the raw name bytes and encode them reversibly with path_text.
- [medium] src/incident/mod.rs:153 — the pipe escape does not escape a backslash that precedes a pipe, so a name like a backslash-pipe-b breaks table columns in summary.md; double backslashes before escaping pipes.
- [medium] src/incident/unknown.rs:68 — the PID-reuse check returns true when a process has no start time, so an unverifiable process can be reported as the parent; return false in that case, matching without_descendants.
- [medium] src/incident/unknown.rs:175 — the hash fallback opens the escaped display path, which can name a different file and record its hash; hash the proc executable handle or leave the hash unavailable for such paths.
- [medium] src/investigation.rs:35 — the registration file is named only by watch, so a second diagnose overwrites the first PID and its Drop deletes the file, leaving the running investigation unexcluded; include the PID in the file name.
- [medium] src/probe/process.rs:28 — the one-second start-time tolerance on Windows can attach a reused PID's command line to the wrong process; compare the native creation time exactly and keep seconds for display only.
- [medium] src/probe/process.rs:73 — every Process32NextW error is treated as end of enumeration, so a failed scan publishes a partial list that can falsely report missing processes; return success only for ERROR_NO_MORE_FILES and propagate other errors.
- [medium] src/commands.rs:360 — the learning-period incident records unknown as 1 while its trigger requires unknown equal 0, so the evidence contradicts the claim; retain the values used for the decision.
- [medium] src/collector/listening_ports.rs:125 — UDP owners and ports are stored in independent sets, so current.json cannot say which application owned which port; keep the port-to-owner mapping and ignore port churn only in the diff.
- [medium] src/commands.rs:500 — the investigation is registered after collection and not at all on dry-run, so a concurrent check can classify the diagnostic process as unknown; register before collection using a per-process record.
- [medium] src/incident/unknown.rs:350 — process-controlled values in table cells keep Markdown image and link syntax active, so opening summary.md can load external content; render these values as literal text in the summary and diff.
- [low] src/collector/listening_ports.rs:117 — when a socket is shared with an excluded PID, the excluded owner is still rendered because identities covers all processes, which contradicts the exclusion goal and makes diffs depend on whether an investigation is running; filter excluded PIDs out of listener.pids before rendering.
- [low] src/probe/process.rs:186 — the whole status file is decoded as UTF-8 to read the ASCII Uid field, so a non-UTF-8 process name drops the UID from the incident; read bytes and decode only the Uid line.
- [low] src/known_set.rs:431 — learn_for is truncated to whole seconds, so the accepted value 500ms disables learning and can mark every running identity as unknown; preserve the precision or reject unsupported precision during validation.
Review complete.

fix: tighten process enumeration and start-time matching

- A non-UTF-8 process name was decoded lossily, so names differing only
  in invalid bytes shared one `name:` identity when the path was
  unreadable. Names are now encoded reversibly like paths, and the
  status file is read as bytes so such a name no longer drops the UID.
- Any Process32NextW error ended the enumeration, so a failed scan
  returned a partial list that could report processes as missing.
  Only ERROR_NO_MORE_FILES ends it now; other errors are returned.
- The one-second start-time tolerance from d5687cb also applied on
  Windows, where creation times do not drift, so a PID reused within
  the second could pass. It now applies only on Linux.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

content.text:
Round 3 of the review asked for changes again, with 16 findings: 14 in code plus the same 2 in `build.ps1`. I fixed all 14 and committed them as 7 commits. Round 4 is now running in the background.

On Windows, clippy and the full test suite pass (283 unit, 12 e2e).

| Commit | What it fixes |
|---|---|
| 1c89827 | Linux process names that aren't valid UTF-8 now get distinct identities, and their UID is no longer lost. A failed Windows enumeration no longer returns a partial list. The ±1 second start-time tolerance now applies only on Linux |
| b25b108 | The summary and diff now escape `\` and the characters that form links and images, so the text renders literally. A process whose start time is unknown is no longer treated as a parent. On Linux, hashes are read only from the running executable itself |
| d475c2f | An investigation is now recorded before it starts collecting, including with `--dry-run`. Records are per PID, so two runs don't delete each other's |
| d823dc1 | `listening_ports` now records which owner held which UDP ephemeral port. Excluded owners are dropped from shared sockets |
| 4f006c8 | A `learn_for` with a fractional second (e.g. `500ms`) is now a config error. It used to be truncated, which turned learning off |
| 4303f4e | When the trigger fires during the learning period, the incident also shows the values the decision was based on |

## Things I'd like you to know
- **Each round turns up new findings in a different area.** The count isn't shrinking: 13 in round 1, 12 in round 2, 14 in round 3. The findings are getting finer-grained, from bugs in the main logic toward edge cases and the evidence format. If round 4 turns up more, tell me whether to keep fixing everything until the review comes back clean, or to stop at a certain severity.
- **I haven't confirmed the Linux code even compiles.** These 3 rounds changed a lot of Linux-only code, and the danger of shipping without even a compile check keeps growing. I'd like to build it in WSL once. Tell me if that's OK, given the free space on C:.
- **I left `build.ps1` alone.** I'll fix it if you ask.
